verdict: M198 closes the M197 preindexed-nonzero oracle at the abstract raw-bitmap schedule level. Its sealed arithmetic is independently reproducible, but the numbers remain a replay opportunity until a stable scanner/compactor and matched finite frontend are proven with Synopsys VCS/DC.

hammer_findings.finding: Full-window early close, token-end partial close, trailing zeros, zero tokens, odd tails, buffer modulo reuse and no-cross-window/token fill all reproduce the sealed schedule exactly.

R4 needs a stable raw-beat scanner and bounded descriptor compactor that proves arbitrary mid-lane early-close residual handling, order preservation, no drop/duplicate, partial-tail flush and ready/valid backpressure. The recurrence does not prove that microarchitecture.

The dual-window queue/head advance, accepted buffer release, token/window/epoch tags, SRAM response latency, stale-response quarantine, Acc24 update and result backpressure remain absent. A matched finite VCS/DC point is required before cycle or area admission.

The fixed close convention is not derived from RTL: empty tokens charge scan+2 while nonempty tokens charge max(scan,drain)+1. Also, every token is fully serialized. These are exact model rules, not measured controller timing.

At R4/B2, stage 0 pair fusion is 0.994911x versus same-width W1 and should be bypassed. A stage-select hybrid would reduce the abstract wall count from 90222444 to 90112890 cycles, only a further 0.1216 percent, so it is a small cleanup rather than a new headline.
Extra buffers have little aggregate value: R4 B2 to B4 saves 0.1576 percent and R8 B2 to B4 saves 0.0858 percent. Do not buy B3/B4 before integrated area/timing evidence.
For B3/B4, the field named fusion_increment_vs_iso_width_w1_b2 mixes fusion with an increased buffer count. Only the B2 decomposition is a clean same-resource fusion comparison.

recommended_next.candidate: R4 raw scanner to bounded F2 stable compactor with stage-0 fusion bypass
recommended_next.why: R4 captures most scanner return while avoiding R8's 768-bit ingress for only 2.56 percent additional abstract wall reduction over R4/B2.
